items.definition:
a curve or recess in a coastline, river, or other geographical feature
The ship sailed into the bight to find shelter from the storm.

a projecting support built against a wall; a source of defense or support
The ancient cathedral was supported by massive stone buttresses.

a slight arch or curve in a surface
The road had a slight camber to allow for water drainage.

the art or science of drawing maps
Modern cartography uses satellite imagery and GIS technology.

the process of releasing, and thereby providing relief from, strong or repressed emotions
Writing in her journal provided a sense of catharsis after the difficult experience.

a part of the brain at the back of the skull
The cerebellum plays a vital role in motor control and coordination.

An action that violates a law, treaty, or code of conduct.
His actions were a clear contravention of the company policy.

The action or process of selling off subsidiary business interests or investments.
The company announced its divestment from fossil fuels.

Liquid waste or sewage discharged into a river or the sea.
The factory was fined for discharging untreated effluent into the river.

The action of going out of or leaving a place.
The building has multiple points of egress in case of emergency.

A possible event or outcome.
We must prepare for every eventuality.

the process of eliminating waste products from the body
The kidneys are vital organs for the excretion of waste.

a member of an international fraternal organization with secret rituals
He was a proud Freemason for many years.

a rooster bred and trained for cockfighting
The gamecock was known for its aggressive nature.

the source of a river or stream
The headwaters of the Amazon River are in the Andes.

supreme power; absolute dominion
The Roman imperium extended across vast territories.

The ability of an organism or cell to move independently.
The doctor tested the sperm's motility.

A mucous membrane.
The lining of the stomach is called the gastric mucosa.

The process of becoming obsolete or outdated.
Technological obsolescence is a major challenge for manufacturers.

The act of pouring a liquid over or through an organ or tissue.
The doctor monitored the blood perfusion to the brain.

A witty remark.
He delivered a witty quip that made everyone laugh.

An act of fitting new or different equipment or parts to something.
The ship underwent a major refit.

Thoroughness and exactness.
The research was conducted with scientific rigour.

A small seal, especially one set in a ring, used to stamp documents.
The king's letter bore his royal signet.

a sudden violent gust of wind or a localized storm, especially one bringing rain, snow, or sleet.
A sudden squall hit the boat, making the waves choppy.

a conjecture; an idea or conclusion that lacks definite proof.
His surmise about the cause of the accident proved to be correct.

a fraudulent scheme or action.
The whole deal turned out to be a swindle.

a person who studies very hard.
He was always considered a bit of a swot in school.

the fact of being done or occurring at a favorable or useful time.
The timeliness of his intervention prevented a disaster.

a medicine made by dissolving a drug in alcohol; a slight trace of something.
She applied a tincture of iodine to the cut.

the quality of being able to be relied on as honest or truthful.
His trustworthiness was never in doubt.

An Orthodox Jewish college or seminary.
He studied at a yeshiva for several years.

An edible mollusc with a shallow, ear-shaped shell lined with mother-of-pearl.
Abalone is considered a delicacy in some cultures.

a person who is very knowledgeable and enthusiastic about an activity, subject, or pastime
As a jazz aficionado, he owned a vast collection of records.

the partial or complete absence of hair from areas of the body where it normally grows
She was diagnosed with alopecia, which caused significant hair loss.

a brittle, crystalline, pinkish-white metallic element
Bismuth is often used in alloys and cosmetics.

a substance capable of causing cancer
Asbestos is a known carcinogen.

a person or thing that classifies
The machine learning model used a powerful classifier.

a prostitute, especially one with high-ranking or wealthy clients
She was known as a famous courtesan in 18th-century Paris.

a device that gives an electric shock to the heart to restore normal rhythm
The paramedics used a defibrillator to restart his heart.

the state of being equivalent or equal in value, amount, function, or meaning
The equivalency of the two degrees was debated.

a person who writes essays
The renowned essayist published a new collection of works.

the condition of being different from the norm; belief in the uniqueness of a nation or group
American exceptionalism is a belief that the United States is unique.

divine nature, deity
The concept of the Holy Trinity represents the three persons of the Godhead.

the killing of an infant
The historical practice of infanticide was often linked to poverty.

vaccination
The inoculation provides protection against the disease.

a person who initiates something
He was identified as the instigator of the riot.

disobedience to authority
The employee was fired for gross insubordination.

an eccentric or crazy person
Some people thought he was a kook because of his strange ideas.

a medicine that helps bowel movements
The doctor recommended a mild laxative for his constipation.

matter; substance
The alchemists sought to transform base materia into gold.

the transfer of a major branch of industry or commerce from private to state ownership or control
The government announced the nationalisation of the railway system.

Flamboyant confidence of style or manner
He played the role with great panache, captivating the audience.

A word formed from a verb and used as an adjective or noun
In the sentence "The running water," "running" is a present participle.

A deviation of a system from its normal state
The unexpected perturbation in the satellite's orbit caused concern.

The study of the sound system of a language
Her research focuses on the phonology of regional dialects.

An agent representing another in legal or financial matters
The procurator was appointed to manage the estate.

A person who insists on absolute adherence to traditional rules
As a language purist, he disliked the use of slang.

the capacity to recover quickly from difficulties; toughness
Her resiliency allowed her to bounce back after the setback.

a type of music that combines rock and roll with country music
Elvis Presley was a pioneer of rockabilly music.

an institution for the care of people with a specific illness or condition
He was sent to a sanitarium to recover from his illness.

the process of settling or being deposited as a sediment
The sedimentation process helps clarify water.

courage and determination
She showed a lot of spunk in standing up to the bully.

ostentatious display of wealth or status
He likes to show off his new car with a lot of swank.
